## §12.1.1–12.1.2: The Mystery of Representational Discontinuity &amp; The 4 Mechanisms {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">EPISTEMIC FIREWALL &amp; STRATUM A/B/C ARCHITECTURE (§12.1.1–12.1.2, FIG. 12.1)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.firewall-box}
**Strict Non-Transfer Principle (Epistemic Firewall):**
$$
\boxed{\mathbf{A}\text{-Mathematical Validity} \;\centernot\Rightarrow_{\text{arch}}\; \mathbf{C}\text{-Cognitive Architecture} \;\centernot\Rightarrow_{\text{arch}}\; \mathbf{E}\text{-Empirical Confirmation}}
$$
Formal derivability ($\Gamma_A \vdash_{\mathcal{F}} c$) certifies internal structural consistency; it neither substitutes for neurobiological testing nor depends on speculative physical claims.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**The Phenomenological–Neurobiological Gap (§12.1.1):**
* **V1** computes localized spatial-frequency decompositions via 2D Gabor wavelets (Hubel &amp; Wiesel 1962); **A1** computes logarithmic tonotopic modulations; **IT** computes affine latent hyperplanes (Felleman &amp; Van Essen 1991).
* Yet consciousness never presents $10^6$ retinal voltages or Gabor coefficients—it presents an **immediate, unified, qualitative gestalt**:
$$
\boxed{\text{Lower Cortical Tiers: Distributed Statistical Syntax} \;\overset{\textbf{Discontinuity}}{\Longrightarrow}\; \text{Conscious Perception: Unified Gestalt}}
$$
* **Two Standard Fallacies:** (1) *Cartesian Display Fallacy* (homuncular screen regress, Dennett 1991); (2) *Linear Pooling Reductionism* ($v_1 \oplus v_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{N+M}$ yields no internal binding or non-linear gestalt).
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-up}
**The Four Formal Mechanisms of Syntrometrie (§12.1.2):**
1. **Operadic Feature Consumption (Ch. 2):** $\Osyn$ consumes lower features via *Episyllogismus* $\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1}$ into coinvariant quotients $F_{\gamma+1}$.
2. **Protosimplex Encapsulation (Ch. 5):** $10^4$-neuron attractor basins in slice $T_n$ collapse to 0D categorical points $\mathcal{P} \in \CSeg(\Xsyn)$ under $\mathbf{M}^n \to \mathbf{M}^{n+1}$.
3. **Non-Abelian Commutators (Ch. 4):** Non-commuting neural timing ($a_i a_j \ne a_j a_i$) generates Lie curvature $\Omegaint = \sum [a_i, a_j] + \dots \ne \mathbf{0}$.
4. **Layered *Strukturkaskade* (Chs. 7 &amp; 9):** Banach contractions compile into the 6D Apex Metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty$ on $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$ (${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+$ kinematics vs. ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ affective agency).
:::

## §12.1.3–12.1.4: Kantian Aesthetics, Carnap's *Aufbau* &amp; Goodman's Critique {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D/A: REFLEXIVE ABSTRAKTION (FIG. 12.2), CARNAP'S QUASI-ANALYSIS (FIG. 12.3) &amp; GOODMAN'S IMPERFECT COMMUNITY (FIG. 12.4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.carnap-box}
**Kantian Transcendental Aesthetics &amp; Heim's *Reflexive Move* (§12.1.3, Fig. 12.2):**
* Kant (*Critique of Pure Reason*, 1781) grounded space and time as pure *a priori* forms of sensible intuition. Heim radicalized this as **anthropomorphe Transzendentalästhetik** (Heim 2000): mistaking our species' sensory filtering and bivalent habits $\{0, 1\}$ for intrinsic ontology fractures continuous reality into artificial *Antagonismen* (wave vs. particle, determinism vs. qualia).
* **Reflexive Abstraktion:** Turns the analytical lens onto observation itself, replacing static $\{0,1\}$ projection with a Grothendieck sheaf topos over structured contexts $U = (P^U, D^U, K^U)$ glued along $\Hol(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P})$ where $\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) = 0$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Carnap's *Aufbau* (1928) &amp; Goodman's Critique (1951) (§12.1.4, Figs. 12.3–12.4):**
* Carnap (*Der logische Aufbau der Welt*, §§67–74) started from the *eigenpsychische Basis* of elementary experiences $e \in E$ and recollected similarity $P_s \subseteq E \times E$ (*Ähnlichkeitserinnerung*), defining **Quality Classes** via **Quasi-Analysis**:
$$
Q \coloneqq \bigcap \left\{ K \subseteq E \;\middle|\; K \text{ is a maximal } P_s\text{-similarity circle and } e_1, e_2 \in K \right\}
$$
* **Goodman's Collapse (*The Structure of Appearance*, 1951):**
  1. **Imperfect Community:** $\{e_1\text{ (Red, Rough)}, e_2\text{ (Red, Round)}, e_3\text{ (Round, Rough)}\}$ satisfy $e_i P_s e_j$ pairwise via *different* qualities; extensional set theory intersects them into a maximal clique, fabricating a **phantom quale**!
  2. **Companionship Difficulty:** A rare quality $Q_1$ co-occurring with pervasive $Q_2$ collapses extensionally into $Q_2$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Sheaf-Theoretic Resolution in the Operadic-Sheaf Model (OSM):**
Replacing set intersections with Kripke–Joyal sheaf semantics over $\Ctx$ equipped with Banach contractions $K^U \colon D^U \widehat{\otimes}_\pi P^U \to C^U$, three pairwise-similar contexts with no common property have trivial triple fiber product:
$$
e_1 \times_U e_2 \times_U e_3 \cong \mathbf{0}_{\Ctx} \implies \mathbf{y}(\mathbf{0}_{\Ctx}) \cong \mathbf{0}_{\Esyn} \implies \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)_{123} \ne 0
$$
The Čech descent defect diverges on the 2-simplex overlap, **rejecting the imperfect community** and rescuing qualia as **sheaf-theoretic descent invariants**.
:::

## §12.1.5–12.1.7: Block's Split, Chalmers' Hard Problem &amp; Zombie Refutation {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A/B: DEFS. 12.1–12.2, CLASS A_12 SINGULARITY (FIG. 12.5), SYNTHESIS (FIG. 12.6) &amp; ZOMBIE IMPOSSIBILITY (THM. 12.3)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Block's Split (1995), Chalmers' Hard Problem (1995) &amp; Categorical Mismatch (§12.1.5–12.1.6):**
* **Block's Dichotomy:** *Access Consciousness* ($A$, functional/reportable) vs. *Phenomenal Consciousness* ($P$, qualitative "what it is like", Nagel 1974; Levine's 1983 Explanatory Gap; Jackson's 1982 Mary's Room).
* **Category Mistake (Fig. 12.5):** Reductive physicalism projects a non-Abelian topos structure onto a scalar $q \in \mathbb{R}$, triggering a **Class $A_{12}$ Dimension-Defect Singularity**: $\dim(F(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{syn}})) < \dim(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{syn}})$.
* **Def. 12.1 ($A$-Consciousness as Free Tree Monad $T_{\mathsf{P}}$):** Typed by cortical levels $\gamma \in \mathbb{N}_0$ over $\Osyn$:
$$
T_{\mathsf{P}}(X) \;\cong\; X \;\oplus_1\; \widehat{\mathsf{P}}(T_{\mathsf{P}}(X)) \quad (\text{Episyllogismus } k\uparrow)
$$
* **Def. 12.2 ($P$-Consciousness as Sheaf Equalizer $\Hol$ &amp; Curvature $\Omegaint$):**
  1. **Holoform Gestalt:** $\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) = 0 \iff \Hol(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P}) \cong \mathbf{P}(U)$.
  2. **Quale as Curvature:** $\Omegaint \coloneqq \sum_{1 \le i < j \le N} [a_i, a_j] + D_{A_0}a_{\mathrm{int}} + \sum_{k=1}^N [a_k, a_{\mathrm{int}}] + \frac{1}{2}[a_{\mathrm{int}}, a_{\mathrm{int}}]$ with Frobenius intensity $g_E = \frac{1}{2}\|\Omegaint\|^2$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.3 &amp; Proof (Formal Impossibility of Chalmersian Zombies):**
Let $\mathcal{N} = (P_U \to M_U, \mathbf{A}, \Osyn)$ execute multi-modal binding across $N \ge 2$ channels. Define:
$$
\mathsf{Zombie}(\mathcal{N}) \iff \big(A\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{True}\big) \wedge \big(P\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{False} \iff \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \equiv \mathbf{0}\big)
$$
**Proof:** Assume $A\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{True}$ and $g_E = \frac{1}{2}\|\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}\|^2 = 0 \iff \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \equiv \mathbf{0}$. For linearly independent channel 1-forms $a_1, a_2$ in a non-Abelian gauge algebra $\mathfrak{g} = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$, $\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \equiv \mathbf{0}$ holds iff $[a_i, a_j] \equiv 0$ ($\forall i \ne j$) and $a_{\mathrm{int}} \equiv 0$, reducing $\mathbf{A}$ to an Abelian Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h} \subset \mathfrak{g}$. Then the carrier pushout $P_1 \boxplusphi P_2$ collapses to the uncoupled $\ell^1$-coproduct $P_1 \oplus_1 P_2$. On overlap $W = V_1 \times_U V_2$, $s_1|_W \ne s_2|_W \implies \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)_{12} = \delta^0(s)_{12} \ne 0 \implies \Hol(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P}) \cong \emptyset$. Without a global section, $T_{\mathsf{P}}(X)$ cannot evaluate cross-color terms: $\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1}(\Osyn \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \bigotimes F_{\gamma_i}) = \{0\}$, contradicting $A\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{True}$! Thus $\llbracket \mathsf{Zombie}(\mathcal{N}) \rrbracket = \bot_\Omega$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §12.1.8–12.1.9: Dialectical Sublation ($\operatorname{Aufhebung}$) &amp; Heyting Mereology {.smaller transition="fade"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A/B: DIALECTICAL SYNTHESIS (THM. 12.4), HEYTING MEREOLOGY (DEF. 12.5) &amp; SEQUENT CALCULUS L_iMSL</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 12.4: Dialectical Concept Synthesis Theorem ($\operatorname{Aufhebung}$, §12.1.8)**
Let $A, B \le \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{asp}}(W)$ be two internal subobjects exhibiting an evaluative antagonism:
$$
\operatorname{Incomp}_{\mathcal{E}}(A, B) \;\coloneqq\; \big\llbracket |\ev_P(A) - \ev_P(B)| > \theta_{\mathrm{tol}} \big\rrbracket \;=\; \top_{\Omega(W)}
$$
Reflexive abstraction models dialectical sublation ($\operatorname{Aufhebung}$) as a functor mapping contradictory context $S_{\mathrm{mod}}(x)$ to successor context $S'_{\mathrm{mod}}(x')$ containing a synthesized composite whole $C \coloneqq \operatorname{Synthesize}(A, B)$ such that:
1. **Internal Consistency:** $\neg \exists A', B' \big(\operatorname{Part}(A', C) \wedge \operatorname{Part}(B', C) \wedge \operatorname{Incomp}_{\mathcal{E}}(A', B')\big)$.
2. **Higher-Level Generator:** $C$ acts as an initial generator for syndrome construction in $\Prop_{k+1}$, proving that cognitive conflict directly drives conceptual intelligence growth.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 12.5: The Internal Heyting Mereological Universe $\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{asp}}$ (§12.1.9)**
Over context $U \in \Ctx$, the mereological universe is the complete Heyting subobject lattice:
$$
\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{asp}}(U) \;\coloneqq\; \Sub_{\Esyn}\!\left(\mathbf{y}(U) \times (\underline{\mathsf{Pred}}_U \sqcup \underline{\mathsf{Qual}}_U)\right)
$$
where parthood is $\operatorname{Part}(A, B) \iff A \le B$ in $\Omega(U)$. Relational coordination strength between qualifier $(d_r, v_{dr})$ and predicate $(f_q, v_{fq})$ is governed by a continuous Archimedean $t$-norm $\chi \colon [0, 1] \times [0, 1] \to [0, 1]$:
$$
\operatorname{Strength}\big((d_r, f_q), U\big) \;\coloneqq\; \chi\big(\zeta_r \cdot \sigma_{dr}(v_{dr}),\; \mathbf{z}_q \cdot \sigma_{fq}(v_{fq})\big) \;\in\; [0, 1]
$$
A pair is actively coordinated iff $\operatorname{Strength}((d_r, f_q), U) > \theta_{\mathrm{coord}}(U)$, satisfying constructive CEM axioms **MSL-M1** and **MSL-M2**.
:::

Dynamic Modality Rules:</b> $(\langle\pi_F\rangle FI)\;\frac{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\bigwedge_{i=1}^m\phi_i\quad (\psi=F_{\mathrm{ops}}(\vec{\phi})\in\Prop_{k+1})}{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\langle\pi_F\rangle\psi}$, $([\pi_F]\text{-Step/Unstep})\;\frac{S(x);[\pi_F]\Gamma\vdash^k[\pi_F]\theta}{k+1;\Gamma\vdash\theta}$

## §12.2.1: Mechanism 1 — Operadic Feature Consumption (*Episyllogismus*) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: OPERADIC EVALUATION (FIGS. 12.7–12.9) &amp; INFORMATION ERASURE THEOREM (THM. 12.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Operadic Feature Consumption via the *Episyllogismus* ($k \uparrow$, §12.2.1, Figs. 12.7–12.9):**
* Higher cortical tiers do **not** maintain an uncompressed pixel buffer of lower sensory arrays. Within the completed colored Banach operad $\Osyn$ (Ch. 2), multi-channel integration across levels is governed by:
$$
\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1} \colon \Osyn(\underbrace{\gamma,\dots,\gamma}_{m\text{ times}};\; \gamma+1) \;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi\; \left(F_\gamma \;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi \dots \widehat{\otimes}_\pi\; F_\gamma\right) \longrightarrow F_{\gamma+1}
$$
* Input activations at tier $\gamma$ (V1 Gabor orientations, spatial frequencies, motion vectors, A1 pitch bands) function strictly as **operands**, projected into the **coinvariant quotient space**:
$$
F_{\gamma+1} \;\cong\; \left(F_\gamma^{\;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m}\right) \Big/ \overline{\operatorname{span}}\big\{u - \sigma(u) \;\big|\; \sigma \in \Sigma_m\big\} \Big/ \mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{relations}}
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.6 &amp; Proof (Operadic Information Erasure Theorem):**
Let $F_\gamma$ be an $n$-dimensional real Banach space representing a lower cortical feature map. Under $\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1}$, input coordinates $(x_1, \dots, x_m) \in (F_\gamma)^m$ are algebraically consumed into the coinvariant quotient. For any $n \ge 2$ and $m \ge 2$, the evaluation kernel satisfies:
$$
\boxed{\dim\big(\ker(\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1})\big) \;\ge\; n^m \;-\; \binom{n + m - 1}{m} \;>\; 0}
$$
**Proof:** The evaluation morphism factors through the symmetrized coinvariant projection $\pi_{\mathrm{sym}} \colon (F_\gamma)^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m} \twoheadrightarrow \Sym^m(F_\gamma)$, whose kernel is spanned by all non-symmetric tensor permutations. In finite dimensions, $\dim(F_\gamma^{\otimes m}) = n^m$ while $\dim(\Sym^m(F_\gamma)) = \binom{n+m-1}{m}$. For all $n \ge 2, m \ge 2$, $n^m - \binom{n+m-1}{m} > 0$. Because $\ev$ factors through $\pi_{\mathrm{sym}}$, $\ker(\pi_{\mathrm{sym}}) \subseteq \ker(\ev)$, erasing individual lower coordinates unless an explicit top-down adjoint section $\ev^*$ is applied. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §12.2.2: Mechanism 2 — Protosimplex Encapsulation &amp; The Metroplex Lift {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SUBOBJECT-MINIMAL PROTOSIMPLEX (DEF. 12.7) &amp; DIMENSION-COLLAPSE THEOREM (THM. 12.8, FIG. 12.10)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Dimensional Chunking via the Metroplex Lift ($\mathbf{M}^n \to \mathbf{M}^{n+1}$, §12.2.2, Fig. 12.10):**
* A distributed, recurrent firing pattern across $10^4$ spiking neurons in the inferior temporal (IT) cortex does not present to conscious awareness as $10^4$ coupled differential equations.
* In the slice category $T_n \coloneqq \operatorname{Met}_n(\Xsyn)/G_n$ of grade-$n$ configurations over blueprint $G_n$, stabilized attractor basins $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$ ($\dot{V} \le -\gamma V$) are encapsulated into atomic 0D objects of the higher-level Hypermetrophor ${}^{n+1}\mathbf{w}\widetilde{\mathbf{a}}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 12.7: Augmented Subobject-Minimal Protosimplex**
Let $T_n \coloneqq \operatorname{Met}_n(\Xsyn)/G_n$ and let $\Alg_{\mathcal{O}_n}^0$ be the category of augmented algebras over the base constant subalgebra $\Free_{\mathcal{O}_n}(\emptyset)$. An object $\mathcal{P} \in \Obj(T_n)$ is a **Protosimplex of Grade $n$** if it is non-trivial and contains no proper non-trivial augmented sub-algebras:
$$
\forall A \hookrightarrow \mathcal{P} \text{ in } \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_n}^0, \qquad A \;\cong\; \Free_{\mathcal{O}_n}(\emptyset) \;\;\vee\;\; A \;\cong\; \mathcal{P}
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.8 &amp; Proof (Protosimplex Dimension-Collapse Theorem):**
Let $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ be a recurrent neural circuit whose state space is a smooth Fréchet manifold $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{circuit}} = C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^k, \mathbb{R}^N)$ possessing an asymptotically stable attractor $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$. If $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ stabilizes into a Protosimplex $\mathcal{P} \in \Obj(T_n)$, then under the nerve embedding:
$$
N_{n+1} \colon \operatorname{Met}_{n+1}(\Xsyn) \longhookrightarrow \operatorname{Cat}_\infty(\Xsyn), \qquad \mathcal{P} \;\in\; \big(N_{n+1}(\mathbf{M}^{n+1})\big)_0 \;\cong\; \Obj(\mathbf{M}^{n+1})
$$
**Proof:** By Def. 12.7, $\mathcal{P}$ contains no proper non-trivial subobjects in $T_n$. In the complete Segal space $\CSeg(\Xsyn)$, the 0-th simplicial degree $X_0$ comprises the objects of the internal category (Hypermetrophor components). Because $\mathcal{P}$ is subobject-minimal, internal trajectories within $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ collapse into degenerate 1-simplices $s_0(\mathcal{P}) \in X_1$, presenting $\mathcal{P}$ as a discrete 0-dimensional point token to $\operatorname{Met}_{n+1}$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.intuition-box}
**Why Complex Chords &amp; Semantic Concepts Feel Indivisible (Fig. 12.10):**
* **Lower Level $n$ ($\operatorname{Met}_n / G_n$):**
  * Attractor Basin $\mathcal{B}(T_{z,1})$ ($10^4$ spiking IT neurons encoding moving vertical stripe contours) $\xrightarrow{\text{Lift}}$ **0D Atom $\mathbf{P}_A$ ("Stripes")**.
  * Attractor Basin $\mathcal{B}(T_{z,2})$ ($10^4$ spiking STG neurons encoding $80\,\mathrm{Hz}$ acoustic harmonics) $\xrightarrow{\text{Lift}}$ **0D Atom $\mathbf{P}_B$ ("Growl")**.
* **Upper Level $n+1$ ($\operatorname{Met}_{n+1}(\Xsyn)$):**
  * The conscious workspace operates **exclusively over these 0D categorical pointers** $\mathbf{P}_A, \mathbf{P}_B \in X_0$ linked by higher relational functors ${}^{n+1}\mathfrak{f}$, explaining why a musical chord or face is experienced as a single indivisible unit rather than a neural ledger.

## §12.2.3: Mechanism 3 — Non-Abelian Commutators &amp; Hodge Qualia Bipartition {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: INTERACTION CURVATURE (THM. 12.9, FIG. 12.11) &amp; HODGE BIPARTITION OF QUALIA (THM. 12.10, FIGS. 12.12–12.13)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 12.9 &amp; Proof (Relative Interaction Curvature Decomposition, Fig. 12.11):**
Let $P_U \to M_U$ be a principal $G$-bundle over $(M_U, g_U)$ with non-Abelian $\mathfrak{g} = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$, and let $\mathbf{A} = A_0 + \sum_{k=1}^N a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}} \in \operatorname{Conn}(P_U)$ across $N \ge 2$ sensory channels. The total curvature 2-form $F_A \in \Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad} P_U)$ decomposes identically as:
$$
F_A \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^N \mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \;+\; \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}, \quad \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \;\coloneqq\; \sum_{1 \le i < j \le N} [a_i, a_j] + D_{A_0}a_{\mathrm{int}} + \sum_{k=1}^N [a_k, a_{\mathrm{int}}] + \frac{1}{2}[a_{\mathrm{int}}, a_{\mathrm{int}}]
$$
**Proof:** Expanding $F_A = d(A_0 + a) + \frac{1}{2}[A_0 + a, A_0 + a] = F_{A_0} + D_{A_0}a + \frac{1}{2}[a,a]$ for $a = \sum_{k=1}^N a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}}$ and grouping single-channel terms under $\mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} = \frac{1}{N}F_{A_0} + D_{A_0}a_k + \frac{1}{2}[a_k,a_k]$ isolates $\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}$. Even when each individual sensory channel is internally flat ($\mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} = 0$), non-commutativity $[a_i, a_j] \ne 0$ generates non-zero interaction curvature with Frobenius intensity $g_E \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}\|\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}\|^2$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.10: Hodge Bipartition of Qualia Energy (Figs. 12.12–12.13)**
On a compact boundaryless context manifold $(M_U, g_U)$, the connection Laplacian $\Delta_{A_0} \coloneqq D_{A_0}D_{A_0}^* + D_{A_0}^*D_{A_0}$ yields the $L^2$-orthogonal Fredholm splitting in $L^2\Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad} P_U)$:
$$
\boxed{\Omegaint \;=\; \underbrace{\Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}}}_{\in\,\operatorname{im}(\Delta_{A_0})\;\text{(Dynamic Flow)}} \;+\; \underbrace{\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}}}_{\in\,\ker(\Delta_{A_0})\;\text{(Topological Core)}} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad g_E = \frac{1}{2}\|\Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}}\|_{L^2}^2 + \frac{1}{2}\|\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2}
$$
* **Dynamic Intentional Qualia ($\Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}} = \Delta_{A_0}G_{A_0}(\Omegaint)$):** Transient focal perceptions, attention shifts, and adaptive sensory updates.
* **Topological Background Qualia ($\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}} \in H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M_U, \operatorname{ad} P_U)$):** Invariant self-presence and baseline embodiment.
:::

## §12.3.1–12.3.2: Structured Contexts $\Ctx$, Seifert–van Kampen &amp; Metropie Flow {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A/B: STRUCTURED CONTEXTS (DEF. 12.12), SEIFERT–VAN KAMPEN (THM. 12.13), PSEUDOMETRIC d_P (DEF. 12.14, PROP. 12.15) &amp; LIOUVILLE METROPIE (DEF. 12.16, THM. 12.17)</div>

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 12.12: The Category of Structured Contexts $\Ctx$ (§12.3.1)**
$\Ctx$ is the small skeleton category in $\FinBan$ whose:
1. **Objects** are tuples $U \coloneqq (D^U, P^U, C^U, K^U, z^U, \zeta^U, \mathcal{S}_D^U, \mathcal{S}_P^U)$ with Predicatrix space $P^U$, Dialectic space $D^U$, output channel space $C^U$, linear contraction $K^U \colon D^U \widehat{\otimes}_\pi P^U \to C^U$ ($\|K^U\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1$), isometric ciphers $z^U \in \operatorname{Isom}(P^U)$, $\zeta^U \in \operatorname{Isom}(D^U)$, and closed convex cylinders $\mathcal{S}_D^U, \mathcal{S}_P^U$.
2. **Morphisms** $\alpha = (\alpha_D, \alpha_P, \alpha_C) \colon V \to U$ are linear contractions satisfying:
$$
\alpha_C(K^V(d, p)) = K^U(\alpha_D(d), \alpha_P(p)), \quad \alpha_P \circ z^V = z^U \circ \alpha_P, \quad \alpha_D \circ \zeta^V = \zeta^U \circ \alpha_D
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 12.13 &amp; Proof (Context Seifert–van Kampen Pushout–Pullback Commutation):**
For a span $W \xrightarrow{\iota_1} U, W \xrightarrow{\iota_2} V$ in $\Ctx$ with overlap $W = U \times_Z V$ and pushout $U \sqcup_W V$:
1. **Colimit Preservation:** $\mathfrak{R}_P(U \sqcup_W V) \cong P^U \boxplusphi P^V \coloneqq (P^U \oplus_1 P^V)/\Im(\delta_\phi)$, where $\delta_\phi(w) = (\iota_{1,P}(w), -\iota_{2,P}(w))$.
2. **Mayer–Vietoris Equalizer in $\Esyn$:** For any sheaf $\mathbf{F} \in \Esyn$,
$$
0 \longrightarrow \mathbf{F}(U \sqcup_W V) \xlongrightarrow{\;\rho^*\;} \mathbf{F}(U) \oplus \mathbf{F}(V) \xlongrightarrow{\;\iota_1^* - \iota_2^*\;} \mathbf{F}(W)
$$
**Proof:** (1) In $\FinBan$, the pushout of contractions is the $\ell^1$-coproduct quotient by $\Im(\delta_\phi)$; naturality of $z^U, z^V, z^W$ induces an isometric cipher on the quotient. (2) Yoneda $\mathbf{y} \colon \Ctx \to \Esyn$ preserves colimits up to sheafification, so $\Hom_{\Esyn}(-, \mathbf{F})$ maps the epimorphic covering sieve $\mathbf{y}U \sqcup_{\mathbf{y}W} \mathbf{y}V \twoheadrightarrow \mathbf{y}(U \sqcup_W V)$ to the exact equalizer $\ker(\iota_1^* - \iota_2^*)$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Discrepancy Metric $d_P$ (Def. 12.14, Prop. 12.15) &amp; Metropie Flow (Def. 12.16, Thm. 12.17):**
* **Def. 12.14 &amp; Prop. 12.15:** $d_P(U, V) \coloneqq \inf_{\alpha,\beta} \max_{F \in \{D,P,C\}} \max(\|I_{F^U} - \beta_F\alpha_F\|_{\mathrm{op}}, \|I_{F^V} - \alpha_F\beta_F\|_{\mathrm{op}})$ satisfies $d_P(U,W) \le d_P(U,V) + d_P(V,W)$ via $\|I - \beta_1\beta_2\alpha_2\alpha_1\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \|I - \beta_1\alpha_1\|_{\mathrm{op}} + \|\beta_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|I - \beta_2\alpha_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\alpha_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}$.
* **Def. 12.16 (Infinitesimal Metropie Metric Tensor):** On $G = \operatorname{Isom}^+(P_n) \cong \mathrm{SO}(n)$, $g_{\mathrm{met}}(\dot{z}_1, \dot{z}_2) \coloneqq -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}((z^{-1}\dot{z}_1)(z^{-1}\dot{z}_2)) \ge 0$.
* **Theorem 12.17 &amp; Proof (Liouville Invariance of Metropie Geodesic Flows):**
  1. **Haar Invariance:** Since $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ is compact and unimodular, 1-parameter geodesic translations $\Phi_t(z) = z\exp(tX)$ preserve Haar measure: $(\Phi_t)_*(d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}) = d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}$.
  2. **Symplectic Liouville Volume:** On $T^*G$ with $\omega_{\mathrm{can}} = dp_i \wedge dq^i$ and $H(z,p) = \frac{1}{2}\|p\|_{g_{\mathrm{met}}}^2$, Cartan's Magic Formula gives $\mathcal{L}_{X_H}\omega_{\mathrm{can}} = d(\iota_{X_H}\omega_{\mathrm{can}}) + \iota_{X_H}(d\omega_{\mathrm{can}}) = -d^2H = 0 \implies \mathcal{L}_{X_H}\Omega^n = 0 \implies \operatorname{div}_{\Omega^n}(X_H) \equiv 0$. Perspective shifts neither compress nor dilate cognitive informational volume! $\blacksquare$
:::

## §12.3.3–12.3.5: Subcanonicity of $\Jsyn$, Čech Cohomology &amp; Obstruction Dichotomy {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A/B: SUBCANONICITY PROOF (THM. 12.18), ČECH COBOUNDARY NILPOTENCY (DEF. 12.19, PROP. 12.20) &amp; OBSTRUCTION DICHOTOMY (THM. 12.21)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.proof-box}
**Theorem 12.18 &amp; Proof (Subcanonicity of the Syntrometric Topology $\Jsyn$, §12.3.3):**
Every representable presheaf $\mathbf{h}_X \coloneqq \Hom_{\Ctx}(-, X)$ is a sheaf in $\Esyn$, and $\Omega(U)$ is a complete internal Heyting algebra ($p \vee \neg p \ne 1_\Omega$):
$$
\Hom_{\Ctx}(U, X) \xlongrightarrow{\mathcal{R}} \prod_{i=1}^m \Hom_{\Ctx}(V_i, X) \rightrightarrows \prod_{i,j=1}^m \Hom_{\Ctx}(V_i \times_U V_j, X)
$$
1. **Injectivity (Separation):** By Def. 12.12, joint addition $\rho_F \colon \bigoplus_{i=1}^m F^{V_i} \to F^U$ admits a contractive split-section $\sigma_F$ with $\rho_F \circ \sigma_F = \operatorname{id}_{F^U}$. If $f \circ \rho_i = g \circ \rho_i$, then $f_F(u) = \sum_i (f_F \circ (\rho_i)_F)(\sigma_{F,i}(u)) = g_F(u) \implies f = g$.
2. **Surjectivity (Gluing):** Given matching $(f_i)_{i=1}^m$, define $f_F \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^m (f_i)_F \circ \sigma_{F,i}$. Contractivity holds since $\|f_F\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \max_i \|(f_i)_F\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\sigma_F\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1$, and cipher naturality holds because $\sigma_P, \sigma_D$ commute with $z^U, \zeta^U$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Čech Complex (Def. 12.19, Prop. 12.20) &amp; Obstruction Dichotomy (Thm. 12.21, §12.3.4–12.3.5):**
* **Def. 12.19 &amp; Prop. 12.20:** On $\check{C}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{A}) = \prod_{i_0 < \dots < i_p} \mathbf{A}(V_{i_0\dots i_p})$, $(\delta^p\omega)_{i_0\dots i_{p+1}} = \sum_{j=0}^{p+1} (-1)^j d_j^*(\omega_{i_0\dots\widehat{i_j}\dots i_{p+1}})$ satisfies $\delta^{p+1} \circ \delta^p \equiv 0$ via simplicial identity $d_j^* \circ d_k^* = d_k^* \circ d_{j-1}^*$ ($k < j$).
* **Theorem 12.21 (The Epistemic Obstruction Dichotomy):**
  1. **Type I Conflict (Evaluative Discrepancies / 0-Coboundaries):** $s \in \check{C}^0$ with $s_i|_{V_{ij}} \ne s_j|_{V_{ij}}$ yields $\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) = \delta^0(s) \ne 0$, but $[\delta^0(s)] = 0 \in \check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{A})$ since $\delta^1(\delta^0 s) = 0$. Resolvable by local context refinement!
  2. **Type II Conflict (Intrinsic Topological Antinomies / Non-Trivial 1-Cocycles):** $g \in \check{Z}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{A})$ with $[g] \ne 0 \in \check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{A}) \iff \neg\exists s \in \check{C}^0$ with $\delta^0(s) = g$. Global Holoform $\Gamma \in \mathbf{A}(U)$ is **topologically obstructed**!
:::

:::

## §12.3.6–12.3.8: Beck–Chevalley, Hereditary Stability $\Stable_k$ &amp; Prime Saturation {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A/B: TRI-ADJOINT QUANTIFIERS (PROP. 12.22), BECK–CHEVALLEY (THM. 12.23), WORKING MEMORY INVARIANCE (DEF. 12.24, THM. 12.25, FIG. 12.17) &amp; PRIME SATURATION (THM. 12.26)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Tri-Adjoint Quantifiers (Prop. 12.22) &amp; Beck–Chevalley Invariance (Thm. 12.23, §12.3.6):**
* **Prop. 12.22:** For every $f \colon V \to U$ in $\Ctx$, pullback $f^* \colon \Sub_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbf{y}U) \to \Sub_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathbf{y}V)$ admits left and right adjoints $\exists_f \dashv f^* \dashv \forall_f$, with $\exists_f(A) \coloneqq \Im(f \circ \iota_A)$ and $\forall_f(A) \coloneqq \max\{B \hookrightarrow \mathbf{y}U \mid f^*(B) \le A\}$.
* **Theorem 12.23 &amp; Proof (Beck–Chevalley Invariance):** Over pullback $W = V_1 \times_U V_2$ with $\pi_1 \colon W \to V_1, \pi_2 \colon W \to V_2$ and $g \colon V_1 \to U, f \colon V_2 \to U$, for every $A \hookrightarrow \mathbf{y}V_2$:
$$
\mathbf{BC}_\exists \colon \;\exists_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*(A)) \;\cong\; g^*(\exists_f(A)), \qquad \mathbf{BC}_\forall \colon \;g^*(\forall_f(A)) \;\cong\; \forall_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*(A))
$$
**Proof:** ($\mathbf{BC}_\exists$) Since $\Esyn$ is a Grothendieck topos, regular images are stable under pullback, so pulling back $A \twoheadrightarrow \exists_f(A) \hookrightarrow \mathbf{y}U$ along $\mathbf{y}g^*$ yields $\exists_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*A) \cong g^*(\exists_f A)$. ($\mathbf{BC}_\forall$) By categorical mates: $\Hom(B, g^*(\forall_f A)) \cong \Hom(f^*(\exists_g B), A) \cong \Hom(\exists_{\pi_2}(\pi_1^*B), A) \cong \Hom(B, \forall_{\pi_1}(\pi_2^*A))$, plus Yoneda. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Hereditary Stability $\Stable_k$ &amp; Working Memory Invariance (Def. 12.24, Thm. 12.25, Fig. 12.17):**
* **Def. 12.24:** Immediate Generative Parthood $\IGP_{j+1}(X, P') \iff (P' = \operatorname{Conj}(X,Y)) \vee (P' = \operatorname{Conj}(Y,X)) \vee (P' = \operatorname{Lift}_{\mathrm{syn}}(X))$. World $(U, k)$ satisfies:
$$
(U, k) \models \Stable_{j+1}(P') \iff (U, k) \models P' \;\wedge\; \forall X\big(\IGP_{j+1}(X, P') \implies (U, k) \models \Stable_j(X)\big)
$$
* **Theorem 12.25 &amp; Proof (Working Memory Invariance):** If $S(x); \Gamma \vdash^k \Stable_k(P)$, then for every $\alpha \colon V \to U$ in $\Ctx$, $U \Vdash P \implies V \Vdash \alpha^*(P)$. Proven by induction on $k$: base $k=0$ uses $\nu_V(\alpha^*a_i) = \Omega(\alpha)(\top_{\Omega(U)}) = \top_{\Omega(V)}$; step $k=j+1$ uses $\alpha_C \circ K^V = K^U \circ (\alpha_D \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \alpha_P)$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.proof-box}
**Theorem 12.26 &amp; Proof (Simultaneous Multi-Level Prime Saturation Theorem, §12.3.8):**
Let $S(x); \Gamma_0 \nvdash^0 \phi_0$ be an unprovable root sequent at level $k=0$. There exists an infinite sequence of Prime Saturated Theories $\mathbf{\Delta} \coloneqq \langle \Delta_k \subset \mathcal{L}_k \rangle_{k \in \mathbb{N}_0}$ linked by the deterministic dynamic transition relation:
$$
(\Delta_k, k) \,R_{\pi_F}^c\, (\Delta_{k+1}, k+1) \;\iff\; \big\{\theta \in \mathcal{L}_{k+1} \;\big|\; [\pi_F]\theta \in \Delta_k\big\} \;\subseteq\; \Delta_{k+1}
$$
satisfying the **Truth Lemma across all levels $k \in \mathbb{N}_0$**:
$$
\boxed{(\Delta_k, k) \models \psi \;\iff\; \psi \in \Delta_k \qquad \forall \psi \in \mathcal{L}_k}
$$
**Proof:** Extend $\Gamma_0$ to a prime $0$-theory $\Delta_0$ with $\phi_0 \notin \Delta_0$ via the Prime Extension Lemma. Inductively, given $\Delta_k$, define $\Theta_{k+1} \coloneqq \{\theta \mid [\pi_F]\theta \in \Delta_k\} \cup F_{\mathrm{ops}}(\Delta_k \cap \Prop_k)$. If $\Theta_{k+1} \vdash^{k+1} \bot$, rule $([\pi_F]\text{-Unstep})$ forces $\Delta_k \vdash^k [\pi_F]\bot \to \bot$, contradicting consistency of $\Delta_k$. Thus $\Theta_{k+1}$ extends to a prime $(k+1)$-theory $\Delta_{k+1}$, and Truth Lemma induction holds on lexicographic rank $\mathbf{m}(\psi) = (\operatorname{rk}(\psi), k)$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §12.4.1–12.4.2: Completed Operad $\Osyn$, Beck Distributive Law &amp; Selection Functors {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A/B: COMPLETED COLORED OPERAD O_syn (DEF. 12.27), BECK DISTRIBUTIVE LAW (THM. 12.28) &amp; SELECTION POWER FUNCTORS (DEF. 12.29)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 12.27: Completed Free Colored Banach Operad $\Osyn$ (§12.4.1)**
Let $E_{\mathrm{pyr}} \in \mathsf{Coll}_{\mathbf{Col}}(\mathbf{Ban})$ be the colored generating collection with operations $E_{\mathrm{pyr}}(\gamma,\dots,\gamma;\gamma+1) \coloneqq \mathcal{B}_{\le 1}((F_\gamma)^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m}, F_{\gamma+1})$ and $\{0\}$ otherwise. The **Completed Free Operad** is:
$$
\Osyn \;\coloneqq\; \widehat{\mathbb{F}}_\pi(E_{\mathrm{pyr}})(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma) \;\coloneqq\; \bigoplus_{[\tau] \in \operatorname{Tree}(\vec{\gamma};\gamma)/\sim}^{\ell^1} \left(\widehat{\bigotimes}_{v \in V(\tau)}^\pi E_{\mathrm{pyr}}\big(\operatorname{in}(v); \operatorname{out}(v)\big)\right)_{\Aut(\tau)}
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.28 &amp; Proof (Inductive Proof of the Beck Distributive Law for Tree Monads):**
Let $(\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}, \mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}, \eta_{\mathrm{pyr}})$ and $(\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}, \mu_{\mathrm{frag}}, \eta_{\mathrm{frag}})$ be the algebraic free tree monads on $\FinBan$. The natural transformation $\lambda \colon \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}} \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \Longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}$ defined by structural recursion:
$$
\lambda_X\big(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}(t)\big) \coloneqq \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}})(t), \qquad \lambda_X\big(\psi(t_1,\dots,t_m)\big) \coloneqq \mu_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\psi)\big(\lambda_X(t_1),\dots,\lambda_X(t_m)\big)
$$
satisfies the **four Beck coherence diagrams** identically:
1. **Unit Law 1 ($\lambda \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\eta_{\mathrm{frag}} = \eta_{\mathrm{frag}}\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}$):** $\lambda_X(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}(\eta_{\mathrm{frag}}(x))) = \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}})(\eta_{\mathrm{frag}}(x)) = \eta_{\mathrm{frag}}(\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}(x))$.
2. **Unit Law 2 ($\lambda \circ \eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} = \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\eta_{\mathrm{pyr}}$):** Holds directly by the base definition.
3. **Multiplication Law 1 ($\mu_{\mathrm{frag}}$ Pentagon):** Naturality of operadic substitution $\psi \circ_i \theta$ commutes with root grafting in $\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}$.
4. **Multiplication Law 2 ($\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}$ Pentagon):** Induction on tree depth + associativity of $\widehat{\otimes}_\pi$ gives $\lambda_X(\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}(T)) = (\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\mu_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \circ (\lambda\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}) \circ (\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\lambda)(T)$, extending continuously via the BLT Theorem to $T_{\mathrm{pyr}}, T_{\mathrm{frag}}$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 12.29: The Four Elementary Selection Power Functors in $\FinBan$ (§12.4.2)**
For an $n$-dimensional carrier space $V \in \Obj(\FinBan)$, the four universal selection functors of arity $m$ are:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{Sel}_{(4)}^{(m)}(V) &\coloneqq V^{\otimes m}, & \dim &= n^m & &\text{(Homometral Asymmetric)} \\
\mathsf{Sel}_{(2)}^{(m)}(V, B) &\coloneqq V^{\underline{\otimes}m}(B), & \dim &= \frac{n!}{(n-m)!} & &\text{(Heterometral Asymmetric)} \\
\mathsf{Sel}_{(3)}^{(m)}(V) &\coloneqq \Sym^m(V), & \dim &= \binom{n+m-1}{m} & &\text{(Homometral Symmetric)} \\
\mathsf{Sel}_{(1)}^{(m)}(V, B) &\coloneqq \Lambda^m(V), & \dim &= \binom{n}{m} & &\text{(Heterometral Alternating)}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Role of the Four Selection Regimes in Cortical Syntax Compression:**
* $\mathsf{Sel}_{(4)}^{(m)}$ preserves full ordered sequence syntax ($n^m$).
* $\mathsf{Sel}_{(3)}^{(m)} = \Sym^m(V)$ drives **Operadic Feature Consumption** (Thm. 12.6), projecting out permutation order to form order-invariant perceptual gestalts.
* $\mathsf{Sel}_{(1)}^{(m)} = \Lambda^m(V)$ drives **Programmable Cognitive Closure (*Syndromabschluss*, Thm. 12.34)**, vanishing identically whenever $m > n$.
:::

:::

::::

Present Section 12.4.1–12.4.2: Definition 12.27 (Completed Free Colored Banach Operad $\Osyn$), Theorem 12.28 (Inductive proof of the 4 Beck coherence laws for $\lambda \colon \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \Rightarrow \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}$), and Definition 12.29 (The Four Elementary Selection Power Functors $\mathsf{Sel}_{(1\dots 4)}^{(m)}$).
:::

## §12.4.3–12.4.5: Carrier Pushouts, Corporate Classes &amp; *Syndromabschluss* {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: CONFLEXIVITY INDEX (DEF. 12.30, FIG. 12.18), PUSHOUT EXACT SEQUENCE (THM. 12.31), CORPORATE DETERMINACY (THM. 12.32), CYCLIC RESONANCE (THM. 12.33) &amp; SYNDROMABSCHLUSS (THM. 12.34)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Conflexivity (Def. 12.30, Fig. 12.18) &amp; Carrier Pushout Exact Sequence (Thm. 12.31, §12.4.3):**
* **Def. 12.30:** On interaction tree $G_{\mathcal{S}} = (V, E_C \sqcup E_K, \Sigma)$, $\operatorname{ConfIndex}_{\mathrm{pres}}(G_{\mathcal{S}}) \coloneqq |E_K| + 1$ ($|E_K|=0$: subconscious Konzenter coproduct $P_a \oplus_1 P_b$; $|E_K| \ge 1$: conscious Exzenter pushout $P_a \boxplusphi P_b$).
* **Theorem 12.31 &amp; Proof (Carrier Pushout Short Exact Sequence):** Let $\dim P_a = p, \dim P_b = q$, and $\delta_\phi(r) = (\phi_a(r), -\phi_b(r))$:
$$
0 \longrightarrow \frac{R_\phi}{\ker\phi_a \cap \ker\phi_b} \xlongrightarrow{\;\bar{\delta}_\phi\;} P_a \oplus_1 P_b \xlongrightarrow{\;\pi_{\boxplus}\;} P_a \boxplusphi P_b \longrightarrow 0
$$
1. **Exactness &amp; Rank–Nullity:** $\ker(\delta_\phi) = \ker\phi_a \cap \ker\phi_b \implies \dim(P_a \boxplusphi P_b) = p + q - \operatorname{rank}(\delta_\phi) = p + q - \lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
2. **Universal Quotient Norm:** $\|[(x,y)]\|_{\boxplus} \coloneqq \inf_{r \in R_\phi}(\|x - \phi_a(r)\|_{P_a} + \|y + \phi_b(r)\|_{P_b})$ satisfies $\|h([(x,y)])\|_Z \le \|[(x,y)]\|_{\boxplus}$ for any contractions $f \circ \phi_a = g \circ \phi_b$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Corporate Classes (Thm. 12.32), Cyclic Holonomy (Thm. 12.33) &amp; Closure (Thm. 12.34):**
* **Thm. 12.32 (Corporate Class Determinacy):** The $2^4 - 1 = 15$ non-empty subsets of $r \subseteq \{K_s, C_s, K_m, C_m\}$ partition into **9 Mixed Classes** ($1+4+4=9$, algebraically deterministic Syntrix algebras) and **6 Pure Classes** ($2+4=6$, underdetermined).
* **Thm. 12.33 (Re-entrant Cyclic Resonance):** Recurrent feedback loops yield first Betti number $\beta_1(G_{\mathcal{S}}) \coloneqq |E| - |V| + k(G_{\mathcal{S}}) \ge 1$ and fundamental group representation $\rho_{\mathrm{loop}} \colon \pi_1(G_{\mathcal{S}}) \to \Aut_{\mathbf{Syn}}(\konflexivsyntrix)$; self-sustaining working memory holds iff $\rho_{\mathrm{loop}}(\gamma)$ is an attracting isometry.
* **Thm. 12.34 (Programmable Cognitive Closure / *Syndromabschluss*):** Under alternating exterior selection $\Lambda^{m_K}(F_{\chi(K-1)})$, if $m_K > \dim(F_{\chi(K-1)})$, then $F_\gamma \cong \{0\}$ for all $\gamma \ge \chi(K)$, enforcing perceptual decision commitment.
